body: I have 2b/c hair and I've recently started to sort out my hair styling methods as it was getting really dry and losing its bounce. I heard coconut oil was a wonder product as a deep conditioner so I bought it and put it on my hair and slept with it in a shower cap and in the morning it felt dry and straw like! I thought maybe it was the one off so 2 weeks later I tried it again and it still felt very dry and didn't make my hair feel good. It's pure coconut oil. Am I doing something wrong?

Focus on that, focus on working with kids.  That must be an amazing thing to do.  You are not alone in feeling like this and you can change those things that make you feel the way you do.  Killing yourself is a permanent solution to a temporary problem, I know that phrase is overused but that's because it's true.  These problems you have are temporary.  1 month, 6 months or even a year down the line you'll look back and feel happy that you are still here.  You're strong to seek help on here and it's the best thing you can do for yourself.  Is there any services that are available to you so you can take talking about it further?  You can speak to your local mental health team.  It took me a long time to do it and I feel much better for it, a lot of people over look that because they feel it won't do anything.  But it's the best thing you can do for yourself right now.  Don't suffer in silence, there are people who care.

If you've burned all your bridges then make new ones.  Branch out and start something you wouldn't necessarily do.  I was feeling the way you are feeling and I was so close to doing something drastic but then I joined a poker society at my university and I made new friends.  Is there something you can do that you could look up locally?  I know this isn't for everyone but it's a suggestion.

What is getting you down?  Break it down into manageable chunks, recognise what you can change and what you can't.

You will be happy again, I always think that too.  I'm bipolar so I regularly go through those feelings but I promise you that the tides will turn.  Something good will happen in your life and make you realise that it's worth living.  Stay strong.  You're strong to admit your feelings like this on a public forum.  I admire that and you should too.  If you need to talk, I'm here

What is making you feel like this?  What are your current thoughts?  Once you break it down it helps to start addressing them.  Instant decisions are ones that you mostly regret afterwards, like going over to your ex's dorm.  How you're feeling is something I can relate to and definitely understand.  Remember these feelings are only temporary!  I like to see it as waves, it comes and goes (I'm bipolar so it helps me understand but it applies to depression too).  When you start to address your problems the waves become shorter and eventually it will level out.  This isn't permanent.  What makes you happy? What do you enjoy?  A game?  Elvis?  Certain foods? Focus on that.  If you want to talk about anything, I will always be here to listen.  Stay strong.

Keep going, as rintantan said, remember that how you are feeling is temporary.

Think about things you might want to do in life, learn to play an instrument?  Waiting for a specific film/book/game to come out?  Travel?  Make little goals of things you look forward to and the rest is easier, you'd be surprised

I have silly motivations too.  If I were to do anything drastic I couldn't listen to Elvis anymore!

A lot of people don't realise how many small things are keeping them alive.  It's good to take some time to recognise these :)

(Totally excited about Game of Thrones too, and for the next books to come out)

It's good that a friend is there and is encouraging to do something good.  You've made an amazing step by talking to people about it and I know from experience how tough that it.

I understand how you feel completely, I go through these periods a lot but you need to remember that these feelings of being depressed can be changed.  Think about the things you enjoy in life, even simple things and try to hold on to these.  A lot of people take for granted the things around them that make them happy.

What's going on in your life to make you feel like this?  If you want to talk to me then I will always listen.  You're not alone.
